extracted.intended_audience: playwrights, screenwriters, and dramatists studying dramatic structure and craft
extracted.subtask_description: Practical and evaluative criteria for writing dramatic works (plays/screenplays): how to structure scenes, manage action and information, and shape a play so it forces the audience to confront its central truth. Emphasizes scene-level objectives, economy, and the necessity of escalating stakes through the middle to a climactic reckoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject of drama: The Lie
rubrics_metrics.description: "The subject of drama is The Lie. At the end of the drama THE TRUTH — which has been overlooked, disregarded, scorned, and denied — prevails."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The dramatist's job is to design a structure in which the audience must reckon with a truth they have been avoiding. When evaluating a play, identify the lie it exposes and whether the work forces a confrontation with that lie.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure determines meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: "Structure determines meaning — character is a function of plot, not vice versa."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create plot that generates character behavior; avoid building scenes around 'interesting' characters that don't serve plot. Assess whether characters exist to serve the dramatic stakes rather than to provide backstory or exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Throughline: every scene must drive the central question
rubrics_metrics.description: "Throughline — every scene must drive the central question."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each scene should advance or complicate the play's central question; cut scenes that do not. Use the throughline to check scene relevance and pacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Middle must intensify the central question (Second Act problems)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Second Act Problems — The middle is the crisis of every play (and most stories). Stories falter when the middle becomes mere stalling between setup and payoff. The middle must intensify the central question."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid a stagnant middle that merely delays the climax. Ensure the second act escalates stakes, compounds obstacles, and deepens the audience's need for answers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scenes as negotiations: want/obstacle/now
rubrics_metrics.description: "Scenes are negotiations — each character wants something; conflict is bargaining."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose each scene around: who wants what from whom; what happens if they don't get it; why now. Evaluate scenes by whether they present clear objectives, opposing desires, and immediate stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cut everything that isn't necessary (brutal revision)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Cut everything that isn't necessary — Mamet is famously brutal with revision."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be ruthless in revision: remove lines, scenes, or beats that don't serve the throughline or escalate stakes. Anti-pattern: sentimental or decorative passages that do not change the play's direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: No exposition for its own sake
rubrics_metrics.description: "No exposition for its own sake — only what's needed in the moment."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid embedding backstory or informational dumps unless they directly affect present action. Prefer revealing necessary information through conflict and action rather than explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drama is about actions, not feelings
rubrics_metrics.description: "Drama isn't about characters' feelings; it's about their actions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show inner states through choices and behavior. Dialogue should function as action (to get something) rather than as exposition of emotion or thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell the truth — avoid hiding from the subject
rubrics_metrics.description: "Tell the truth — the audience can sense when the writer is hiding from their own subject."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be honest about the play's stakes and implications. Avoid evasive turns that obscure the central lie or dodge the necessary moral or dramatic reckoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspense as withheld answer to a question
rubrics_metrics.description: "Suspense = withheld answer to a question we want answered."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generate and sustain suspense by posing clear questions and delaying their resolution. Evaluate whether the audience wants the answer and whether the drama strategically withholds it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid backstory; prioritize present action
rubrics_metrics.description: "Avoid backstory; what matters is the present action."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus scenes on what characters do now rather than what happened before. Backstory that doesn't alter present decisions should be removed or reworked into present-tense stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control of information: audience vs. character knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality test: "What does the audience know vs. what do the characters know?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manage who knows what to create dramatic irony, tension, and surprise. Use differences in knowledge to structure revelations and to heighten the impact of the climax.

rubrics_metrics.name: Climax must force reckoning with the lie
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality test: "What's the lie the play exposes? Does the climax force a reckoning with that lie?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ending should compel the characters (and audience) to confront the central lie; evaluate whether the climax resolves or meaningfully confronts that lie rather than offering a facile or unrelated payoff.
